nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
That is: let it not bring about distraction (al-lahw) in you, as though it were from «ألهيتُه فلها» (I distracted him, and he became distracted), as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 488-
ومثلك حبلى قد طرقت ومرضع ... فألهيتها عن ذي تمائم محول
(Many a one like you, pregnant, have I visited by night, and many a nursing mother, and I distracted her from her year-old infant wearing amulets.)
وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ: that is, those who are cheated of mercy and reward.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ: it has been said that this indicates that one does not say "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provided him with it" except of what is lawful. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ: an answer (jawāb). وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position (mawḍiʿ) of the fāʾ, not to what comes after the fāʾ. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr read «وأكونَ» (وأكون) in the accusative (naṣb), conjoining it to what comes after the fāʾ. It has been reported that this is how it is in the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd: «وأكونَ» (وأكون); however, it contradicts the written text of the codex (al-sawād) by which the proof has been established. Some of them argued for it, saying: the wāw is dropped in such cases, just as one says «كلمن» and it is written without a wāw.
It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] countered this view, the evidence that it is not sound being that the writing of the codex in parallel cases is otherwise, such as يكون, تكون and نكون, all written with the wāw in the nominative and accusative positions alike, and nothing else is permissible. Someone else said: the case of «كلمن» is different from this, because the wāw was only dropped from it since they wanted to show that the form of the wāw was connected; so since it had already come in «هوّز» they did not need to repeat it; likewise they did not write it in their saying «أبجد». As for ordinary speech, none of this is permissible. Nor is there any need for it, because conjunction to the position (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-mawḍiʿ) is found frequently in the speech of the Arabs. Sībawayh said: had the fāʾ not been there, it would have been jussive (majzūm), meaning: because it is the answer to the interrogative that carries the sense of a wish (tamannī). As the poet said — someone other than Sībawayh recited it: [al-Wāfir] 489-
فأبلوني بليّتكم لعلّي ... أصالحكم وأستدرج نويّا
(So grant me your favour, that perhaps I may make peace with you and draw my journey back.)
And Sībawayh recited, concerning conjunction to the position: [al-Ṭawīl] 490-
فإن لم تجد من دون عدنان والدا ... ودون معدّ فلتزعك العواذل
(If you find no father below ʿAdnān, nor below Maʿadd, then let the blamers restrain you.)
Because the meaning of «من دون عدنان» is «دون عدنان». And he recited: [al-Wāfir] 491-
معاوي إنّنا بشر فأسجح ... فلسنا بالجبال ولا الحديدا
(Muʿāwiya, we are human beings, so be gentle; we are not mountains, nor iron.)
] And likewise his saying: [al-Kāmil] 492-
لا أمّ لي إن كان ذاك ولا أب
(Let me have no mother, if that is so, and no father.)
And likewise his saying: [al-Sarīʿ] 493-
لا نسب اليوم ولا خلّة ... اتّسع الخرق على الرّاقع
(No kinship today and no friendship; the rent has grown too wide for the patcher.)
— conjoined to the position; if you bring it according to the wording you say «ولا خلةً». Similar to it from the Qur'an is مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ [al-Aʿrāf: 186], conjoined to the position of the fāʾ, and with the nominative conjoined to what comes after the fāʾ. The origin of فأصّدّق is «فأتصدّق»: the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād, and this was good because they are in one word and because they are close to each other. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: «فأصّدّق» "and I would give alms (and purify myself)" and وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ "I would perform the Hajj". Someone else said: "I would be among the righteous" means "I would perform the obligatory duties and avoid the forbidden things". The implied form is: "and I would be righteous, one of the righteous".

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَلَنْ يُؤَخِّرَ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُها: accusative (manṣūb) by «لن» according to Sībawayh. According to al-Khalīl, its origin is «لا أن», and it is reported from him that no verb is put in the accusative except by «أن», whether implied or overt. Sībawayh refuted that on the grounds that one may say:
«زيدا لن أضرب» (Zayd I will not strike), but one may not say «زيدا يعجبني أن تضرب» (Zayd it pleases me that you strike), because [Zayd] is inside the ṣila (relative clause) and so cannot precede.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: In my view, «زيدا لن أضرب» is not permissible, because «لن» is not inflectable (lā yataṣarraf), so nothing connected with what it governs may precede it, just as «زيدا إنّ عمرا يضرب» is not permissible; and «لم» is likewise in his view. I related this to Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] and he rejected it, saying: no one has said this. Abū ʿUbayda claimed that some of the Arabs make the jussive with «لن», but this is not known. يُؤَخِّرَ is with hamza, because its origin is from «أخّر», and the hamza is written as a wāw even though it has fatḥa, for two reasons. One of them is that before it is a ḍamma, and the ḍamma prevails because of its strength. The other is that it may not be written as an alif, because what precedes an alif can only be with fatḥa. Whoever lightens the hamza turns it into a wāw and says «يؤخّر». If it is asked: why is it not made "between-between" (bayna bayna)?
The answer is that if it were made between-between, it would be inclined towards the alif, and that would be an error, because what precedes an alif can only be with fatḥa. إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُها: with both hamzas fully pronounced; if you wish you may lighten [one]. Abū ʿAmr drops [one] because [the other] indicates it, since their vowels are the same and the hamza stands on its own. وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ: that is, possessed of full awareness of your deeds, so He records them against you and will requite you for them. The order of speech is that the preposition and its genitive noun should come at the end, because they are an explanation (tabyīn); if any of that comes first, it is intended to be at the end. For this reason the grammarians agreed that one may not say «لبستُ ألينها من الثياب» (I wore the softest of them, of the garments), because the preposition and its genitive noun are at the end in their proper place, so they cannot be intended as coming first. The correct form of the example is «لبس من الثياب ألينها». If you take «ما» to mean «الذي» (which), then the hāʾ is omitted, i.e. «خبير بما تعملونه» (aware of what you do it); it was omitted because of the length of the noun. If you take «ما» as maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), you need no omission, i.e. "and Allah is possessed of full awareness of your doing".

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِذا is in the position of an accusative by جاءك, except that it is not declined, because of its shifting [reference] and because at its end there is an alif, and the alif takes no vowel. The response to إذا is قالُوا نَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ: «إن» is given kasra because of the entry of the lām; and the speech was cut off, so إنّ came at the start and was given kasra. وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لَكاذِبُونَ: the name of Allah the Exalted is repeated overtly because that is more majestic. It is said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, gave them the lie regarding what they concealed. Among the soundest of what has been said about it is that they declared that their own selves firmly held faith while they were lying, so Allah gave them the lie.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is their swearing by Allah that they are indeed of you; and Qatāda said: a shield, by which they protect their blood and their property. Al-Ḥasan read اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ [Translator's note: i.e. إِيمانَهُمْ, "their faith", with kasra; the print shows the standard vowelling], i.e. their profession of belief, as a covering with which they cover themselves just as one covers oneself with a shield in war; so killing them and taking their offspring captive was prevented, because they displayed faith. فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: the object may be omitted, i.e. they turned people away; and the verb may be intransitive, i.e. they turned away from the way of Allah, i.e. His religion with which He is pleased and His law with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ. إِنَّهُمْ ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ: of their swearing to lies and their hypocrisy. «ما» is in the position of a nominative according to the view of Sībawayh, i.e. "evil is the thing", and in the position of an accusative according to the view of al-Akhfash, i.e. "evil is it as a thing which they do".

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ذلِكَ is in the position of a nominative, i.e. that swearing and hypocrisy is because they آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا فطبع على قلوبهم. Assimilating the ʿayn into the ʿayn is permissible, and not assimilating is better because of the remoteness of the ʿayn's place of articulation. فَهُمْ لا يَفْقَهُونَ truth from falsehood nor right from wrong, because of desire's dominance over them.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَإِذا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسامُهُمْ: all the grammarians permitted the jussive by إذا and that it be treated as one of the particles of requital (conditional particles), because it only occurs with a verb and needs a response, and so it is with the particles of requital. Al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Kāmil] 484-
واستغن ما أغناك ربّك بالغنى ... وإذا تصبك خصاصة فتجمّل
(Be content with wealth as long as your Lord enriches you, and when need befalls you, bear it with dignity)
 And another recited: [al-Basīṭ] 485-
نارا إذا ما خبت نيرانهم تقد
(A fire that blazes whenever their fires die down)
 The preference according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ is not to use the jussive with إذا, because what comes after it is timed (muwaqqat), so it differs from the particles of requital in this, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 486-
وإذا تكون شديدة أدعى لها ... وإذا يحاس الحيس يدعى جندب
(When there is a hardship, I am called for it; and when the ḥays is being mixed, Jundab is called)
 وَإِنْ يَقُولُوا تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ, because their speech is like the speech of the people of faith. كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ i.e. they do not understand, and they have no understanding or knowledge, so they are like timber. This [khushubun] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza; and Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read خشب with the shīn quiescent [khushbun], and Abū ʿUbayd inclines to it, claiming that he does not know faʿala [Translator's note: i.e. faʿala-t, the singular خَشَبة] being pluralized on fuʿul with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake and an attack on what the multitude has transmitted. That is not free from one of two aspects: either خشب [khashab] is the plural of خشبة, as in their saying ثمرة and ثمر, so it would be other than what he said about faʿala being pluralized on fuʿul; or it is as the skilled grammarians said: خشبة and خشاب, like جفنة and جفان, and خشاب and خشب [khushub], like حمار and حمر. Moreover, أكمة, أكم and أكم, and أجمة and أجم have been heard. As for خشب [khushb], its original may be khushub, with the ḍamma dropped because of its heaviness; and it may be — and this is better — like أسد and أسد [usd] in the masculine. Sībawayh said: and like خشبة and خشب is بدنة and بدن, and like it in the masculine وثن and وثن [wuthn]. He said: and it is a reading. I reckon that whoever interpreted Sībawayh['s words] "and it is a reading" to mean «كأنّهم خشب» [is mistaken], because his saying "and it is a reading" is a weakening of it; rather, as is said, he means: «إن تدعون من دونه إلّا وثنا» [Translator's note: i.e. وُثُناً], and this is an anomalous reading narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās. يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ i.e. because of their cowardice and the paucity of their certainty, and because they conceal disbelief: whenever revelation came down they were alarmed lest they had been exposed. هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ, because their tongues are with you and their hearts with the disbelievers, so they are spies for them; and عدو has the meaning of أعداء (enemies). فَاحْذَرْهُمْ قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ i.e. He punished them and destroyed them, so they became like one who has been killed. أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ i.e. from where are they turned away from the truth after the proofs have become manifest?

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: this is on the basis of giving governing effect to the second verb, just as you say:
أقبل يكلمك زيد; if you gave governing effect to the first you would say أقبل يكلمك إلى زيد, and تعالوا يستغفر لكم إلى رسول الله. لَوَّوْا رُؤُسَهُمْ [Translator's note: i.e. لَوَوْا, without doubling, as the following contrast requires] may be for a small number, and لوّوا for multiplicity. وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ i.e. turning away from going to the Prophet ﷺ so that he might seek forgiveness for them.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ is in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the meaning is: seeking forgiveness and not doing so. لَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ, because they are disbelievers. The Prophet ﷺ only sought forgiveness for them because outwardly they were Muslims, so the meaning of his seeking forgiveness for them was: "O Allah, forgive them if they are believers." إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ: it is said: i.e. He does not grant them success; and it is said: He does not guide them to the reward and Paradise.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: يَنْفَضُّوا i.e. they disperse. Qatāda said: the one who said this was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; he said: "Were it not that you spend on them, they would leave him and abandon him." Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «هم» refers to them and to whoever held his view. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is better than the view of whoever said that «هم» refers to one person. وَلِلَّهِ خَزائِنُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ i.e. in His hand are the keys of the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, so no one gives anyone anything except by His permission, nor withholds it except by His will. وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لا يَفْقَهُونَ that this is so; and for this reason they say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ: al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ related that it is read لنخرجنّ الأعزّ منها الأذلّ with the nūn, and that this means "we shall surely drive out the mighty from it, abased" [Translator's note: i.e. with الأذلَّ as a ḥāl]. Al-Farrāʾ related: ليخرجنّ الأعزّ منها الأذلّ [Translator's note: i.e. layakhrujanna, "the mightier will surely go out from it, abased"], also in the meaning of "abased" (dhalīlan). Most grammarians do not permit the ḥāl to have the alif and lām, except that Yūnus permitted مررت به المسكين, and Sībawayh related دخلوا الأوّل فالأوّل; but these are things on which the Qurʾān may not be construed — except that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «ليخرجنّ» may operate like لتكونن, so that its khabar is definite. الأعز and العزيز are one, i.e. the strong, the secure, the unassailable, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 487-
إذا ابتدر القوم السّلاح وجدتني ... عزيزا إذا بلّت بقائمة يدي
(When the people rush to their weapons, you find me mighty once my hand has gripped the hilt)
 It is also narrated «منيعا», and the meaning is the same. وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ i.e. and so they said this.
